key_insight: Solid-solution stability in refractory complex concentrated alloys is strongly inherited from binary interactions, enabling composition-based design of robust single-phase or tunable multiphase microstructures.
engineering_relevance: Composition-space maps can guide alloy selection beyond equimolar compositions, with Ti, Ta, Nb, and Mo generally favoring solid solutions and Cr and Zr favoring precipitation or segregation.
method: Use rapid, first-principles-based thermodynamic phase-field calculations to map solid-solution stability across nine refractory alloying elements.
Quantify stability using percentage miscible region across ternary, quaternary, and quinary systems.
Analyze binary inheritance and element-specific effects on higher-order miscibility.
evidence_signal: Benchmarking against 109 experimentally reported quaternary-to-senary compositions produced through diverse processing routes achieved 80% overall classification accuracy.
watch_item: The 80% benchmark accuracy leaves meaningful classification uncertainty; candidate compositions still require experimental validation under intended processing conditions.
paper_title: First-principles-based Prediction of Phase Fields: Part II. Solid Solution Tunability in Refractory Complex Concentrated Alloys
